A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAPE study. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on UltraInteract, Tulu–Olmo, OpenHermes and Magpie-Zoo, together with self-distillation and other analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated selection baselines, long-chain-of-thought experiments, token-weighted training and iterative GRAPE results.

M1.justification: The main response-selection procedure is retained, but Appendix B.4 introduces a distinct training objective that weights token losses by token likelihood. Appendix G also adds iterative selection using the fine-tuned checkpoint before another training round. These extend the procedure beyond selecting responses followed by standard SFT.

E1.justification: Appendices B.3–B.4 add long-chain-of-thought training using an OpenR1-Math/LUFFY subset and OpenThoughts-114k. Evaluation expands to AIME24/25, AMC, Minerva, OlympiadBench, ARC-C, GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro. OpenHermes coverage is retained through relocation to Appendix B.2.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds evaluated LESS and Emb-NV baselines for all three target models. Appendix B.1/Table 7 adds response selection using Skywork-Reward-Llama3.1-8B-v0.2. LESS was discussed in v1's related-work appendix but was not an evaluated comparator there; the original comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: The original main experiments retain their reported one-epoch training and learning rate. Added experiments introduce Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B configurations, a second selection-and-training round, and a study sampling 1,000 Tulu instructions. The new LESS comparison specifies four warmup epochs on 5% of the data and 8192-dimensional gradient projection.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and Appendix H newly examine how response-source preferences differ across base models. Appendix G tests whether selection remains useful after initial fine-tuning, while Appendix B.4 tests extending likelihood-based supervision to token losses. The earlier single-generator, self-distillation, parameter-distance and UltraInteract subset analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests for its experimental results. v3's checklist invokes greedy pass@1 evaluation, but this adds no uncertainty estimates or statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: The original benchmark results are retained, but v3 adds substantial results for new comparators and experiments. Table 9 reports Qwen2.5-1.5B MATH accuracy of 0.396 with GRAPE versus 0.330 with highest-perplexity selection. Table 10 reports token-level GRAPE versus baseline scores of 60.20 versus 55.60 on MATH, but 3.23 versus 4.38 on AIME-25. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The computational-cost definitions, assumptions and derivations in v1 Appendix E are retained in v3 Appendix F. No new theorem or proof is introduced. The standard perplexity formula added in Section 3.2 explains score computation without adding a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central claim remains that matching supervision to the target model's distribution improves SFT performance and efficiency over stronger-teacher responses, larger datasets and existing selection approaches. The headline gains in the abstracts are retained; the additional experiments support this existing claim.

C2.justification: v3 Section 7 explicitly qualifies GRAPE's applicability by candidate-pool quality and the base model's inherent capabilities. It also explains that response selection can complement instruction-level selection. These are useful qualifications beyond v1's existing warning about self-generation and reduced diversity.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the Question/Answer scoring template and length-normalized log probabilities in Section 3.2. Appendix C adds LESS and NV-Embed implementation details, and the checklist discloses greedy pass@1 evaluation. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments; the GPU and batch-size disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and discussion concerning SPIN, newer data-selection work by Dai and Ivison, NV-Embed, and long-chain-of-thought resources. It clarifies complementarity with instruction selection. The underlying positioning of GRAPE as model-dependent response selection remains stable, as does most of the detailed selection-method survey.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, experimental introductions, baseline descriptions and conclusion. Related work is integrated into the background, OpenHermes moves to the appendix, and the single-generator and self-distillation discussions become an ablations section. Dedicated discussion/limitations, acknowledgments and a conference checklist further reorganize the document.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column formatting with extensive figure and table repositioning. The original three figures are retained and rearranged; a response-selection heatmap is added. Table 2 gains comparator rows, four new result tables appear, and the OpenHermes table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central empirical argument by supplementing v1's S2L and data/response controls with gradient-based, embedding-based and reward-based selection comparisons. The model-specific selection analysis, clearer scoring instructions and explicit applicability limits also improve assessment of the method. Uncertainty remains unquantified, and some new reporting overstates the evidence: Appendix B.1 claims superiority on every benchmark despite Table 7's Mistral length-controlled win rates of 13.6 for GRAPE versus 13.9 for reward selection. These localized weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger comparative evidence.
